newsitem.title: UK: Unilever suffers 50 mln stg currency hit.
newsitem.headline: Unilever suffers 50 mln stg currency hit.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch consumer group Unilever Plc/N.V. suffered a 50 million stg hit from the strength of sterling on foreign exchange markets in the three months to June 30, said chief press officer Mike Haines on Friday.

"The impact of sterling's strength, excluding the foreign exchange effect from the sale of speciality chemicals, was about 50 million negative in the quarter and about 70 million in the year to date," said Haines in an interview.

Earlier, the company announced an unexpectedly sharp rise of 37 percent in pre-tax profits for the second quarter to 836 million stg, excluding profit on the sale of its speciality chemicals division.
Unilever sold its speciality chemicals business to Imperial Chemical Industries Plc in early July for $8.0 billion.
The leap in profits sent the group's shares 37p higher to 1803p by 0830 GMT. Analysts had forecast profits in a range of 730 to 780 million stg.
However, analysts expressed some disappointment in the poor sales growth of one percent in the second quarter and a weak outlook from the company.
"For the first time in a number of years the net effect of acquisitions less disposals has had a negative impact on sales and reduced sales growth by one percent," said Haines.
"However, the underlying volume of continuing business, excluding speciality chemicals, grew by two percent," he added.

So far this year the group has sold its speciality chemicals business, the professional haircare business of Helene Curtis, maple syrup firm Mrs Butterworth and its Nordsee fish restaurant, wholesale and retail business and John West Foods.
"In our developing and emerging markets, sales increased buy eight percent but fell by one percent in developed markets due to disposals during the quarter," said Haines.
Analysts also said they were impressed by the strong margin improvement, especially in Europe.
"Overall margins in Europe improved and the region continued to benefit from cost savings," said Haines.

Margins in Europe rose to 12 percent in the second quarter up from 9.5 percent over the same period last year. Trading profit from the region increased to 484 million stg over the same period from 385 million.
Earnings from the group's Asia and Pacific businesses also improved strongly to show a 23 million increase to 105 million in the second quarter.
However, the company gave a very cautious outlook, with chairman Niall Fitzgerald saying profits growth in the remainder of the year was expected to be less buoyant.
